text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
ROMANIA LIBERA
- The Romanian Oil Company will be listed on the Bucharest stock exchange.
- The central bank will support Romania's exports by deprciating the local leu currency, the paper says.
- The government issued an order allowing private farmers to get new credits even if they failed to pay back old loans.
- Romania will contribute some 91 billion lei to the international peacekeeping force in Albania.
- The new customs bill will take effect starting May 1.
- The government approved the bill on bank privatisation.
ADEVARUL
- The bill on bank privatisation will be endorsed by parliament by the end of April, the paper quotes Reform Minister Ulm Spineanu as saying.
- Trade unions in the health sector staged a protest protest rally in Bucharest on Monday.
- Astra Vagoane SA rolling stock marker in Arad threatened by lack of orders.
- The sugar industry could be seriously affected if the government fails to support the sector, the paper says.
- The accord between Romania and the IMF will be signed on April 22, the central bank said.
- Some 6,000 workers at the Roman SA truck factory went on strike.
- Rivers in southern and eastern Romania reached flooding levels.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- The South African Breweries firm plans to invest some $30 million in Romanian breweries.
- Ships owned by Romania's fishing fleet are sold as scrap iron, the paper says.
General:
ROMANIA LIBERA
- Defence Minister Victor Babiuc says in an interview that Romania not joining NATO would cause a disapointment among the population and cost the country more than its admission.
- Austria will smooth Romania's way towards the European Union, says Austrian Foreign Minister Wolfgang Schuessel in an interview ahead of his visit to Bucharest on Wednesday.
- The newspaper presents some of Romania's centuries-old monuments which need protection and funds for maintenance.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- Romania's former King Michael will spend Romanian Orthodox Easter in the western city of Timisoara.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- More than half of Romania's young people do not know how to use modern contraceptive methods, said the national centre for mother and child protection.

- A meeting between the Romanian and Ukrainian Presidents would be a step forward to consolidate our relations, said Romanian Foreign Minister Adrian Severin on a suggested meeting between Leonid Kuchma and Emil Constantinescu. -- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
